text:
[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved historical episodes where the tape looked like KWEB on 2026-09-18, the median realised 10-session return was 0.68%, with a standard deviation of 8.19%. The single number to anchor on is that median: in half of these analogs the name finished slightly higher over two trading weeks, and in half it finished lower, but the dispersion around that midpoint was wide enough to include outcomes from -9.23% to 43.14%.

[state]
The engine selected these 50 analogs because KWEB currently sits in a distinctive combination of deep price depression and thin liquidity. The distance from the 52-week high (dist52) is -42.74%, carrying a z-score of -1.899, meaning the ETF is far below its recent peak in a way that rarely happens. At the same time, the 20-session dollar-volume regime z-score (dv20z) is -2.663, with a clipped z-score of -1.607 used for retrieval, indicating unusually low trading volume. The 20-session return (ret20) is -6.97% (z-score -0.828), and the drawdown from the 60-session peak (dd60) is -14.73% (z-score -0.792). These features are weighted heavily in the "name" group, which carries 30% of the distance metric. The macro backdrop also pulls specific history into the neighborhood: WTI crude changed by 19.24% over 20 days (oilChg20, z-score 1.124), while benchmark 20-session volatility (mktVol20) is relatively quiet at 9.16% (z-score -0.574). The retrieval spans from 2016-12-14 to 2026-09-03, pulling 35 distinct sessions across 28 symbols, with only 4 instances of KWEB itself due to a mandatory 10-session gap between same-symbol matches.

[history]
Over the 10-session horizon, the 50 analogs produced a mean return of 1.81% and a median of 0.68%. The distribution is highly right-skewed (skew 2.601), driven by a single massive outlier: NIO on 2025-07-08 returned 43.14%. Without that episode, the upside tail is much thinner. In 56% of the analogs the 10-session return was above zero; in 44% it was below. The 10th percentile outcome was -5.81%, and the worst realised return was -9.23%. Looking at the histogram, the most populated bin is centered at 0.59% (18% of the analogs), followed by the bin at -1.59% (12%) and 2.77% (14%). The bad tail is dominated by recent weakness in consumer and China names. The closest analog, KWEB itself on 2026-08-31, fell -5.15%. NKE on 2026-09-03 dropped -8.41%, and PDD on 2026-08-31 fell -7.05%. Older analogs were generally milder: TMO on 2016-12-14 lost -1.61%, and AMZN on the same date lost -0.48%.

[tails]
A position can end near the median and still experience severe intra-horizon pain. Across the 50 analogs, the median maximum adverse excursion was -3.3%. The 10th percentile of max adverse excursion reached -7.26%, and the 25th percentile was -5.96%. On the upside, the median max favourable excursion was 4.04%, with the 75th percentile at 8.43% and the 90th percentile at 14.31%, yielding a reward-risk ratio of 1.22. For drawdown breaches during the 10 sessions, 32 of the 50 analogs experienced a 5% drawdown at some point. Only 2 analogs breached a 10% drawdown. None breached 15% or 20%. This means that while moderate dips were common, catastrophic intra-horizon path risk was rare in this specific conditional set.

[stress]
The stress scenarios reveal how this baseline distribution shifts under specific regimes. The 2025-04 tariff shock is the most damaging relevant scenario: the median forward return drops to -3.36% (a delta of -4.04% versus baseline), the 10th percentile hits -17.57%, and 65.4% of those analogs breached a 10% drawdown. Its caveat is that policy reversals inside the window make the tail asymmetric in a way specific to that episode. The 2020-02/03 liquidity crash yields a median of -9.75% (delta -10.43%), a 10th percentile of -23.23%, and a 75% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown. Its caveat is that central-bank backstops arrived inside the window, so the rebound is baked into the returns; it is a sample of one regime, not a forecast. The 2024-08-05 carry unwind produces a median of -2.77% (delta -3.45%) and a 10th percentile of -10.02%, with a 22.2% breach rate. Its caveat is that the reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, so terminal returns look benign even though intra-horizon excursions did not. The 2022 inflation/rate bear shows a median of -4.81% (delta -5.49%) and a 30% breach rate. Its caveat is that a nine-month window means the per-date cap of 2 analogs samples it repeatedly; treat it as a regime description, not 50 independent events. The 2018-Q4 tightening scare gives a median of -3.08% (delta -3.76%) and an 8% breach rate. Its caveat is that it ended with a policy pivot in January 2019, flattering late-window analogs. Conversely, the 2023-03 regional bank stress actually improved outcomes, with a median of 4.4% (delta 3.72%) and zero 10% drawdown breaches. Its caveat is that the very short window means the analog set is dominated by a handful of sessions. Shock-based stresses like the volatility spike (+2 sigma VIX) show a median of 0.67% (delta -0.01%), but its caveat is that VIX shocks mean-revert quickly, stressing entry timing more than terminal value. The earnings release day stress shows a median of -1.25% (delta -1.93%) and a 20% breach rate; its caveat is that foreign private issuer dates come from noisy 6-K full-text search. No scenarios were skipped by the engine.

[limits]
This analysis has concrete limits. The validation block states explicitly that analog retrieval hits its 80% coverage target out of sample (achieving 83.6% on 2627 test queries), but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage, registering a -2.4% deficit in matched coverage sharpness versus the same-name benchmark. Furthermore, the raw probability integral transform (PIT) distribution fails a uniformity test (chi-square 306.6 against a critical value of 16.92). The engine's own honest verdict is that this is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source. The conformal interval width is 24.44% (from -11.54% to 12.9%), reflecting the high variance of the analog set. The dataset relies on keyless API pricing and SEC full-text search for earnings, which introduces noise. Finally, the extreme skew of the baseline distribution is heavily dependent on a single NIO observation, meaning the right tail is fragile to the removal of one data point.
